verdict.reason: Verified the claim end to end. In cmdReview the `--fresh` deletion is gated on `!dryRun` (spec-to-pr.mjs:954), so under `--dry-run` no round directory is removed and `roundsOnDisk(base)` (line 949) returns the same value before or after the rmSync loop. The only test of the new bound logic (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:702-744) routes all three invocations through a helper that hardcodes `--dry-run` (line 718), so the read-before-delete ordering that the fix and its docblock (spec-to-pr.mjs:946-949, 974) exist to establish is never exercised: moving line 949 below line 958 leaves the test green while restoring the real-run bypass. I searched wide for a counterexample: every `--fresh` occurrence in the repo outside node_modules/lockfiles is spec-to-pr.test.mjs:239 (pure roundDirsToClear unit test), :448 (`--dry-run --fresh`), :702-736 (dry-run bound test) and usage/doc strings in spec-to-pr.mjs; no `--fresh` in .github/workflows or any shell script. Every CLI `review` invocation is at test lines 365, 448, 517, 535, 718, 779 and the only non-dry-run one (line 535) carries no `--fresh` and asserts only `--rebuttals` errors. No source-text/ordering assertion test exists for spec-to-pr.mjs (unlike the source-regex style at review-panel.test.mjs:3292), and rounds.mjs/rounds.test.mjs "fresh" hits are about rerun budgets, not round deletion. The dry-run test is not wholly vacuous — it does kill a mutation of the spentRound expression — but the real-run ordering invariant, whose failure silently lets a 4th round present as round 1 past the bound and discard carry-forward verdicts, has no covering test. Gap is real and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric (silently weakened guard).

finding.summary: Test "a forged `infra` key cannot suppress a finding" passes for the wrong reason and asserts the opposite of the contract
finding.evidence: The fixture at prior-findings.test.mjs:507-514 carries `infra: true` AND `lane: "backlog"`. In `carryForwardFindings` the `f.lane !== "backlog"` filter (prior-findings.mjs:159) runs before the projection, so the record is dropped by the lane rule; the assertion `deepEqual(..., [])` at line 516 holds whether or not the `infra` ordering fix exists. The inline comment ("It is dropped as an infra record only because of the forged key") is therefore false, and the test's title/assertion directly contradict the sibling test at line 528-537, which asserts the same forged-`infra` shape IS carried. As written this test would keep passing if the infra filter were moved back before the projection — i.e. it provides zero coverage of the very regression it is presented as guarding — and it documents the suppression behaviour as desired, inviting a future "fix" that reinstates the bug.

verdict.reason: The described test does not exist. The forged-`infra` test at scripts/agent/prior-findings.test.mjs:549-563 uses the fixture `{ severity: "critical", file: "a.ts", summary: "a real finding", infra: true }` (line 555) with NO `lane` key, and asserts the finding IS carried (lines 556-558) — not `deepEqual(..., [])`. Lines 507-514 cited by the reviewer are the comment block of the separate projection test, which explicitly documents that it avoids a `lane: "backlog"` fixture for precisely the vacuity reason raised (lines 509-512); line 516 is `line: 12`, not an empty-array assertion. Lines 528-537 are that test's expected object, not a contradicting sibling test. The lane rule has its own isolated test at 541-547. The forged test is non-vacuous: `isInfraRecord` short-circuits on `f.infra === true` (prior-findings.mjs:58), and the infra filter runs after the projection that strips `infra` (prior-findings.mjs:166-192), so moving the filter back before the projection — the exact regression claimed to be unguarded — would make the assertion at 556 fail. A grep of the whole test file shows no fixture combining `infra: true` with `lane: "backlog"`.
